description: Team PyroSync is building an Earth Science & Software solution for the Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge. We combine Python geospatial modeling, interactive web visualization, and NASA FIRMS satellite data (MODIS 1 km & VIIRS 375 m) to build a 2000–2026 Burning Activity Calendar for wildfire and climate monitoring.
summary: PyroSync is an interactive web application and Python geospatial harmonization engine that unifies 26 years of NASA FIRMS active fire observations from MODIS (1.0 km resolution on Terra and Aqua, 2000–2026) and VIIRS (375 m I-4 and 750 m M-13 resolution on Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21, 2012–2026). Because VIIRS 375 m pixels have a ~7.1x smaller nadir footprint than MODIS 1 km pixels and higher sensitivity to small and nighttime burns, raw hotspot counts jump 3x to 4x after 2012. PyroSync eliminates this artificial sensor discontinuity by filtering South Atlantic Magnetic Anomaly nighttime noise, projecting both sensor records onto an equal-area 1-km sinusoidal grid, reconciling hybrid Fire Radiative Power (MW), and generating a 2000–2026 Burning Activity Calendar with Z-score anomaly alerts and CSV export for wildfire responders and scientists.
details: What It Does & How It Works: Satellite active fire records are split between MODIS Collection 6.1 (1.0 km² nadir footprint, starting Nov 2000 on Terra and Jul 2002 on Aqua) and VIIRS Collection 2 (375 m I-4 band with a 0.36 x 0.38 km = 0.1368 km² nadir footprint to 0.78 x 0.80 km scan-edge footprint across a 3000 km swath, starting Jan 2012 on Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21). Directly summing both sensors produces a 3.5x post-2012 counting jump. PyroSync solves this in two integrated components: 1. Spatiotemporal 1-km Sinusoidal Fusion Engine (harmonize_firms.py): Screens out South Atlantic Magnetic Anomaly (11°E–110°W, 7°N–55°S) low-confidence nighttime alarms and sub-30% MODIS noise, projects coordinates onto an equal-area 1 km x 1 km spherical sinusoidal grid (R = 6371.0088 km), fuses co-located MODIS+VIIRS hits on the same UTC date into 1.0 harmonized cell-day with averaged hybrid 750 m M-13 and MODIS 4-um Fire Radiative Power (MW), and scales VIIRS-only sub-pixel detections (alpha = 0.28) with scan-angle footprint normalization. 2. Interactive Burning Activity Calendar Web App (pyrosync_harmonizer_app.html): Displays a 27-year x 12-month (2000–2026) heatmap with accessible colorblind-safe ramps (Inferno, Viridis, Cividis), 5 regional presets (including Eastern India & West Bengal Corridor) plus custom Latitude/Longitude bounding boxes, monthly Z-score anomaly alerts against the 2000–2025 median, a live CSV pixel-to-grid fusion workbench, and one-click CSV download. Tools & Coding Languages Used: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript (ES6+), Chart.js 4.4.1, Python 3, Matplotlib, and NumPy.
projectRefs: NASA Earthdata FIRMS MODIS C6.1 & VIIRS 375m C2 Active Fire Data
